examples.scenario: Model poisoning attack on a facial recognition ML model by injecting maliciously crafted images into the training dataset to degrade recognition accuracy for a specific individual class.

training_log_excerpt: 2024-05-15T14:23:47Z WARNING Detected anomalous gradient updates in layer conv3_2: gradient norm spike from 0.032 to 0.54
2024-05-15T14:23:50Z INFO Model accuracy on validation set dropped from 92.4% to 87.1%

anomaly_detection_alert.description: Unusual gradient norm spikes detected during training near batch 1200 on label 'employee_123'. Potential data poisoning suspected.

indicators: Presence of images with suspiciously similar labels but anomalous hash values
Gradient norm spikes in specific model layers during training
Sudden drop in model validation accuracy after ingestion of new training batches
Anomaly alerts triggered by ML monitoring tools on training metrics
Embedded imperceptible adversarial perturbations detected in training images
examples.detection_method: Continuous monitoring of training metrics including gradient norms and validation accuracy; hashing and comparing new training data files; implementing anomaly detection on training data distribution and model performance metrics; manual inspection of flagged suspicious images using image forensics tools; applying adversarial training and robust statistics to identify poisoned samples.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1610 - Deploy Containerized Machine Learning Models (for deployment phase monitoring)
T1621 - Multi-Stage Channels (poisoning during training pipeline)
